aggregate_zig.rounding_rule: rounded to nearest integer for the requirement table; unrounded value preserved here for audit

evidence.basis: all-fragments (Zig-only shard; common-basis figure requires merge across all 10 language shards per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule — this shard reports Zig's own raw counts and a provisional all-fragments score pending that merge)

counting_methodology.counting_rule: For each Zig fragment (measured_fragment only, per R5), an annotator checks off exactly one tally per checklist category in which a semantically material behavior CAN occur at that fragment without being signaled by the fixed local surface syntax, under toolchain_binding.recipes and the frozen safety_mode_clause (Zig pinned to -OReleaseSafe: overflow and bounds checks ON, i.e. checked traps). A behavior is NOT counted as hidden if the fixed local syntax makes it unambiguous under the Zig language specification (e.g. explicit `undefined`, explicit `&`/`.*`, explicit `+%`/`@divTrunc`, explicit `try`/`catch`, explicit `defer`, explicit `extern`/`export`, explicit `?T`/`orelse`). Per-probe tally is an integer 0-9 (one checklist item may fire at most once per probe fragment; multiple constructs firing the same category inside one fragment are not double counted). Every count is itemised below with the specific construct and category that fired, so the figure is auditable, per the freeze requirement in semantic_compression.md section D.
counting_methodology.no_double_count_rule: A single underlying rule counted once in Semantic Determinacy/Locality evidence is not re-counted twice inside Hidden Semantic Cost merely because it also appears in the semantic_fact taxonomy; each checklist tally here corresponds to a distinct hidden BEHAVIOR at the construct, not a restatement of a semantic_fact_kind.

limitations_and_next_steps: This is a single-language (Zig) shard. capability_universe.json's interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule requires metrics A-D to be computed PRIMARILY on the probe set for which ALL TEN languages have a fragment (common basis), with the all-fragments figure (reported here) published as a secondary figure alongside each language's n_L and the delta between bases.

The score above (98) is Zig's all-fragments-basis Hidden Semantic Cost score. It must be reconciled against the common-basis score once the other nine languages' shards are merged by the runner; if F05.P3 or any other Zig-NONE probe is FULL/PARTIAL for all nine other languages, that probe drops out of the common basis and Zig's common-basis figure will be computed over 43 (or fewer) shared probes, which may shift this number slightly.

Per-probe hidden_count values and the itemised construct/category pairs are preserved above so a reviewer can re-derive the aggregate mechanically, per spec 6.1.7 and the D-metric freeze-before-annotation requirement.
evidence.n_L_note: 43 of 44 frozen probes have a Zig fragment (FULL or PARTIAL). F05.P3 is NONE for Zig (no closure/function-value construct capable of capturing an enclosing local; Zig functions cannot capture outer-scope variables per the language spec) and therefore carries zero tokens/facts and is excluded from the A-D fragment set, consistent with capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics and na_policy NA-4.

per_probe_zig_hidden_counts.notes: `const n: i32 = 7; return n;` — binding, mutability, type all locally explicit; no hidden behavior.
`var counter: i64 = 0; const LIMIT: i64 = 100;` — var/const distinction is explicit surface syntax.
`var v: i32 = undefined;` then branch-assign both arms — `undefined` is an explicit, locally evident initialization-state marker.
`var buf: [16]u8 = undefined;` — explicit uninitialized-storage marker, not hidden.

`x += 1;` traps on overflow only because the frozen recipe pins -OReleaseSafe; the operator's checked-trap behavior is not recoverable from the `+=` syntax alone without knowing the build-safety mode. Category: context_dependent_overflow_or_numeric_behavior.

`xs.items[1] = 42;` — out-of-bounds would trap; the possibility of a runtime bounds-check failure is not signaled by ordinary index-assignment syntax. Category: implicit_exception_or_failure_propagation.
`var port: *i32 = &slot; port.* = 9;` — explicit address-of and explicit dereference; writable alias fully signaled at the site.
`const window: []const i32 = xs.items[0..];` — explicit const-slice syntax signals both non-copy and read-only.
Pointer identity via `first == second` on `*Handle` values — pointer comparison is the ordinary, locally evident equality form for pointer types in Zig.

Bare call `f(x)` where `x` is an ArrayList/struct value: whether a struct copy occurs at the call boundary is not visible at the ordinary call-site syntax. Category: implicit_allocation_copy_move_destruction_cleanup.
`fn put(cell: *i32) void { cell.* = 12; }` plus call `put(&cell);` — explicit pointer parameter and explicit address-of at call site.
`fn mid(xs: []const i32) i32 { return xs[1]; }` — returns a copied scalar; independence is evident from the scalar return type.
Struct return `{ q: i32, r: i32 }` — explicit two-field struct, no hidden multiplicity.
`const r = a * b + c;` — checked-trap-on-overflow behavior again depends on the pinned safety mode, not on the expression syntax. Category: context_dependent_overflow_or_numeric_behavior.

`@divTrunc`, `@rem`/`@mod`, and float division are explicit builtins/casts, but division-by-zero trap behavior for the integer forms is not signaled at the call site. Category: implicit_exception_or_failure_propagation.
`const o = m +% 1;` — Zig's wrapping-add operator `+%` explicitly names its own overflow discipline at the site (rung ii of the preference order); no hidden behavior.
Explicit local guard `if (b == 0) 0 else @divTrunc(a, b)` — fallback path is written out, not hidden.
`std.mem.eql(u8, s1, s2)` — explicit named function, not an operator; no possibility of dynamically dispatched equality hidden behind `==`.
`std.sort.sort(i32, xs.items, {}, lessThanDesc)` explicit in-place sort with named comparator; in-place mutation of `xs.items` is evident from passing the slice directly.
`std.math.cast(i32, big)` returns `?i32` — explicit optional-returning checked conversion.
`const sum = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(i)) + d;` — Zig requires an explicit cast for every mixed-type arithmetic operand; no implicit conversion exists to hide.
`const e = xs[i];` — ordinary indexing syntax gives no local signal that an out-of-range `i` traps at runtime. Category: implicit_exception_or_failure_propagation.
`const part = xs.items[1..4];` — Zig slice syntax explicitly denotes a non-copying view over existing storage.
`var o: ?i32 = null; const n = o orelse 0;` — explicit optional type and explicit coalescing operator.

Zig's standard library has no optional map/chaining combinator, so the fragment is written with an explicit `if (o) |v| h(v) else null` construct (P-a substitution); the short-circuit is fully visible in the explicit conditional, so no hidden cost is added.
`fn parse_twice(s: []const u8) !i32 { return (try std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10)) * 2; }` — `!i32` return type and `try` both explicitly signal possible failure and propagation.
`const n = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10) catch 0;` — explicit `catch` names the handled failure path.
`const Shape = union(enum) { Circle: f64, Rect: struct { w: f64, h: f64 } };` — closed tagged union, explicit and exhaustively enumerable.
`switch (s) { .Circle => |r| ..., .Rect => |wh| ... }` with no else — compiler enforces exhaustiveness; visibly closed dispatch.

Zig tagged unions cannot be extended from a separate unit; the nearest standard mechanism is a manually-authored vtable/fat-pointer 'interface' struct (the pattern used by std.mem.Allocator). The dispatch through the vtable's stored function pointer is not evident at the call site `shape.area()`-style call; it looks like an ordinary field/method access. Category: overload_or_dynamic_dispatch_not_locally_evident. Scored PARTIAL under P-a.
`fn head(comptime T: type, xs: []const T) T { return xs[0]; }` — explicit comptime type parameter, monomorphized; the T-to-result relationship is visible in the declaration.

Zig has no declaration-site trait/concept syntax; `max_of` relies on comptime duck-typing checked only at instantiation (P-c: guarantee not documented at the declaration). This affects Semantic Determinacy, not Hidden Semantic Cost, since the comptime requirement is still surfaced (as a compile error) rather than silently misbehaving; hidden_count 0.

No interface/abstract-element-type facility exists for heterogeneous runtime dispatch; the nearest standard construct is again a manually authored vtable struct. The call `items[0].tag()`-style syntax does not locally reveal that dispatch runs through a stored function pointer rather than a normal field access. Category: overload_or_dynamic_dispatch_not_locally_evident.
Explicit `for (xs.items) |v| { total += v; }` accumulation loop — fully visible iteration and mutation.

`std.StringHashMap` entry iteration plus `.get("b") orelse 0` — the lookup-miss fallback is explicit; iteration-order non-determinism is a documented library property surfaced separately under Semantic Determinacy rather than an unsignaled hidden behavior at this construct.
`const f = try std.fs.cwd().openFile(...); defer f.close(); ...` — `defer` explicitly marks the scoped release point, including on the error path via `try`.

Zig has no automatic end-of-lifetime hook; cleanup requires an explicitly written `defer handle.deinit();` at each use site (P-a/P-d substitution). Because the release is written out explicitly, no hidden cost is added, but the automatic-and-exactly-once guarantee the probe names is not provided by the language itself.
`const std = @import("std"); std.debug.print("x\n", .{});` — explicit import, explicit call.
`pub fn pub_add(...) ...` vs non-pub `fn secret() ...` in `util.zig`, called as `util.pub_add(2,3)` — visibility explicitly marked with `pub`.
`std.Thread.spawn` plus explicit `.join()` on both handles — thread creation and join points are both explicit in the fragment.
`std.Thread.Mutex` with explicit `.lock()`/`.unlock()` around each increment — synchronization discipline fully visible at the mutation site.
`extern "c" fn abs(i32) callconv(.C) i32;` — `extern`/`callconv(.C)` explicitly mark the foreign boundary and ABI.
`export fn add2(a: i32, b: i32) callconv(.C) i32 { return a + b; }` — `export`/`callconv(.C)` explicitly mark the C-ABI export.
